title: Observability: FIPS_NOT_ALLOWED_E not named in ioctl error log
description:
crypto2dev_to_wc_err() maps EACCES → FIPS_NOT_ALLOWED_E and then emits: 'crypto2dev: ioctl failed errno=%d (wc_err=%d)'. The wc_err field contains the numeric value of FIPS_NOT_ALLOWED_E but the string 'FIPS' or 'FIPS not allowed' does not appear anywhere in the log.

Trigger: the device returns EACCES from any ioctl (cipher INIT, HMAC INIT, FINALIZE, etc.). This happens when the kernel FIPS provider fails its power-on self-test or when the operation is blocked by FIPS policy.

Bad outcome: a support engineer debugging 'TLS handshake fails with FIPS_NOT_ALLOWED_E' must know that wc_err=N (numeric) maps to FIPS_NOT_ALLOWED_E without a wolfSSL error code table. The existing message for the FIPS-probe failure at init time (wc_crypto2dev_init REQUIRE_FIPS path) does say 'FIPS provider not available'; per-operation FIPS violations should be equally named. The fix is to add an explicit 'FIPS not allowed' string to the EACCES case in crypto2dev_to_wc_err, separate from the generic errno/wc_err message.
